clues: This city stands on the River Thames, a wide river that flows to the North Sea. It sits in the south east of a big island in the west of Europe.
The streets and crowds of this huge city trap heat in its dense centre. It can feel far warmer there than in the suburbs, an island of heat.
Royal clerks once rode from town to town with the king and his court. In the 1100s they settled for good here, and rule stayed put.
Bright red buses roll over the bridges here, past black taxis with lit signs on their roofs. The red bus has grown into a loved sign of this city.
The United Kingdom is ruled from this city, by its parliament and its chiefs. Both have sat in the west end for hundreds of years.
